brand.name: Apoyo Food
brand.tagline: Food made by independent creators in Trinidad & Tobago.

footer.legal: Apoyo Food is part of the Apoyo ecosystem. Cooks keep their own kitchens, prices and customers.

comingSoon.phaseNote: Planned for phase {phase} of the build.

requestOrder.title: Requesting an order
requestOrder.description: You will pick items and quantities, choose pickup, delivery or a meet-up, and propose a date and time that fits the cook's availability. Nothing is charged here: the cook confirms first, and payment happens between the two of you.

buyerOrders.title: Your orders
buyerOrders.description: Every request you make will live here with its status — waiting on the cook, accepted, ready, completed — along with the agreed price and the conversation thread for the details.

messageSeller.title: Talking to a cook
messageSeller.description: Messaging is built into an order rather than sitting on a profile, and it translates itself between English and Spanish. That is on purpose: it keeps pickup addresses and phone numbers out of public pages and inside a conversation that only starts once a cook has accepted your request.

buyerAccount.title: Your account
buyerAccount.description: Saved addresses, your language, notification settings and your Apoyo profile will live here. You can browse the whole marketplace without an account — you are only asked to sign in when you commit to something.

sellerListings.title: Your listings
sellerListings.description: Each dish gets its own page: photos, what it costs (a fixed price, a starting price, or price on request), how many people it feeds, dietary tags, and when it is available — a standing weekday schedule, a pre-order lead time, or a date range for a season.

sellerStories.title: Fresh Today
sellerStories.description: Post what came out of your kitchen today in a few taps: a photo, a line about it, and optionally the dish it belongs to. It appears at the top of the home page for the people who follow you and disappears on its own.

sellerOrders.title: Orders from buyers
sellerOrders.description: Requests arrive here with what was asked for, when it is wanted and how it should be handed over. You accept — setting the price if the dish is quote-based — or decline, and the conversation for the details opens once you have accepted.

sellerInsights.title: What people are looking for
sellerInsights.description: What buyers in your areas searched for, what they found nothing for, and which of your dishes get looked at and saved. Apoyo Food has been recording this since the marketplace opened, so the picture will already have history in it when this arrives.

filters.title: Filter meals

styleGuide.title: Sobremesa components
styleGuide.intro: Every primitive from the component library, rendered against dummy data. This page is a build tool, not a storefront page — it is deliberately unlinked, and it is what scripts/verify-a11y.mjs drives at two widths in both locales.

notes.everyStub: Every key in lib/coming-soon.ts, rendered. Each trigger stamps data-coming-soon on itself so a later audit can check the stub inventory against a rendered page.
notes.media: The photos below are synthetic, but they are pushed through the real Slice 4 ingest pipeline — variants, EXIF strip and blur placeholder — and served by the real storage driver, so the blur-up is the production path rather than a mock.
notes.availability: Part F3 asks for ink on a -vivid fill. Only gold-vivid clears AA at this size (6.55:1); green-vivid measures 3.10, terracotta-vivid 3.64, teal-vivid 3.80. Stamps therefore use the text-safe accent — a cream label on the accent fill (5.44-5.72:1), or the accent on its own soft tint for the large market stamp (4.52-4.72:1).
notes.freshToday: Rounded-rectangular cards, never circular rings. Teal freshness dot, the availability window on the card, and seen/unseen as a border treatment.
notes.skeletons: Never a spinner on a browse surface — skeletons plus blur-up only.
notes.rail: Snap-scrolling, full-bleed on mobile, and focusable so it is reachable without gestures.

signedOut.body: The seller workspace needs an Apoyo account. Sign in on any Apoyo site with the account you already use, then come back to this page — the same session works everywhere in the ecosystem.

become.title: Sell your food on Apoyo
become.body: Home cooks, bakers and caterers set up a kitchen here: a profile with your service areas, the languages you cook and talk in, your specialties and your photos. Registration takes one field. Everything after it can be finished later.
become.closed: Seller registration is not open yet. It will appear here the moment it is.

pending.label: Pending review
pending.body: Your kitchen exists and is yours to fill in, but it is not visible to buyers yet — an Apoyo admin reviews new kitchens before they appear in the marketplace. Nothing is blocked in the meantime: keep filling in your profile, and the more complete it is, the faster a review goes.

active.label: Live
active.body: Your kitchen is live in the marketplace. Buyers can find you in browse, search and the seller directory.

suspended.label: Suspended
suspended.body: Your kitchen is hidden from the marketplace. You can still edit everything here; contact Apoyo if you think this is a mistake.

onboarding.title: Set up your kitchen
onboarding.intro: One field to start. Everything else — photos, your story, service areas, languages, specialties and how you hand food over — comes after, one step at a time, and you can stop and come back whenever you like.
onboarding.displayNameHint: This is the name buyers see. Your web address is made from it once and never changes afterwards, even if you rename the kitchen later.
onboarding.privacyBody: Apoyo Food never shows or stores your home address. Buyers see the areas you serve — nothing finer than that. Where to collect an order is something you share yourself, in that order's conversation, after you have accepted it. Photos are stripped of hidden location data the moment you upload them.

setup.title: Finish your profile
setup.intro: Every step saves on its own and every step can be skipped. Come back whenever you like — this page picks up where you left off.

photo.title: Profile photo
photo.body: A photo of you, your kitchen or your best-known dish. This is the small round image buyers see beside your name everywhere on the site.

cover.title: Cover photo
cover.body: The wide banner at the top of your profile. A table, a spread, a work-in-progress shot — something that shows what eating your food feels like.

bio.title: Your story
bio.body: Who cooks here, and what makes it worth ordering. Write it in the language you actually speak — buyers reading the other one get an automatic translation where it matters.

areas.title: Service areas
areas.body: Where you can realistically deliver, meet or have people collect from. Up to three. This is the only location Apoyo Food ever shows publicly.

languages.title: Languages
languages.body: Which languages you can be reached in. Buyers see this before they order, and order messages translate themselves either way.

specialties.title: Specialties
specialties.body: The dishes you are known for. These help people find you in search, spelled however people around here actually spell them.

fulfillment.title: How you hand food over
fulfillment.body: Pick every option you are willing to offer. You can change this at any time, and you agree each order's details in that order's conversation.

gallery.title: Photo gallery
gallery.body: A few shots of past work, on your profile beneath your listings. Optional — but it is what convinces someone who has never ordered from you.
